summary: An excerpt from a fiction book (Book 11, part 109) in which Rebecca Randall and Emma Jane banter about a mortgage that Rebecca sketches as a fiendish villain threatening her family's farm. The conversation then turns to Rebecca's uncertain career plans, whether she should be a writer, editor, or missionary, and she voices doubts about missionary work while Emma Jane argues that God is present everywhere and will reach the heathen in time.
one_line: Rebecca Randall and Emma Jane joke about a farm mortgage, then debate Rebecca's future career and whether missionary work is needed among the heathen.
key_facts: Rebecca Randall cries that the weariness is mutual and that she wishes she had never gazed upon the face of the mortgage.
Emma Jane observes that a note has a 'face,' and says she didn't know a mortgage had one.
Rebecca says the mortgage on the farm is twelve hundred dollars, which she calls a small one.
Rebecca says John once saw a man mortgaged for twelve thousand dollars.
Rebecca sketches the mortgage as a cross between a fiend and an ogre, holding an axe uplifted in his red right hand.
In the sketch, a figure with streaming black locks, meant as a likeness of Rebecca, is staying the axe blow above a tiny house with a weeping family in front of it.
Emma Jane asks whether Rebecca will be a writer or an editor, as if one only had to choose.
Emma Jane suggests Rebecca go out as a missionary to Syria, as the Burches keep urging, and says the Board would pay her expenses.
Rebecca says she cannot make up her mind to be a missionary and does not 'feel a call,' as Mr. Burch says one must.
Rebecca says she is not good enough and does not want to teach people how to live when she has not learned herself.
Emma Jane argues that God is always present and ready, so He can't miss people, and the heathen will find Him eventually.
Emma Jane says God will make allowances for the heathen because hot climates make people lazy and slow, and parrots, tigers, snakes and bread-fruit trees distract them.
Emma Jane asks what happens if the heathen die first, and the excerpt breaks off there.
